notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model, reviewed_by is null; no hardware was attached and no hardware or Isaac Sim run is claimed. Only the catalogue classes cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used (the card's candidate classes), so there are no catalogue requests. The card's family-config/GymnasiumDriver decision was used unchanged: VecEnvRLGames exposes Gym-style reset/step and the RLTask Box spaces, so the Gymnasium bridge can express the interface. The card's mock_strategy.preferred is upstream-sim, but the simulator is Isaac Sim 4.0.0, installed outside the clone and started with its own python.sh (README.md:31-33); it is not available where the gate runs and package code never imports the clone, so the package fake is used and no sim backend is offered. The fake is an analytic F0 stand-in written for this repository, not a copy of the exemplar; its action/observation sizes, reset ranges, reward, failure thresholds, 500-step limit and control period cite the clone, and its two velocity gains are marked placeholder test data. NOT COVERED: the vectorised per-environment arrays (Cartpole defaults to num_envs 512, Cartpole.yaml:8; the real step returns per-env reward and reset tensors plus an observation dict with obs and states), rendering/cameras, domain randomisation, the states buffer and the PhysX rigid-body dynamics; the fake serves one environment, so reward and done are scalars and the observation is a four-vector. The fidelity gaps name these differences and say the fake was never compared with an Isaac Sim run. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge only records the seed for the next reset), four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived inputs (seed twice, ticks, and action.values; the bridge publishes no unit for them and the normalised action value is dimensionless), and two G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space and observation_space, which come from VecEnvBase outside the clone (vec_env_rlgames.py:34). G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. The check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the check printed for the last run.
